transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Rajiv (IronPeak CTO), Sofia (ML Lead), Tom (Infra)

Summary: Quick vendor-exit discovery; customer currently on OpenAI + vLLM for some on-prem inference; main asks are parity (quality + latency), cost forecast for dedicated, and private deployment options for sensitive data. Security/compliance and a reproducible benchmark are top priorities.

Topics: migration strategy; eval parity (TGI/vLLM parity); Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private; KV cache and prefix caching behaviors; quantization and perf; networking/VPC and KMS; rollouts and canary testing.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, quick intros?
00:08 Rajiv: sure, Rajiv here, CTO at IronPeak, we run a mix of hosted OpenAI for chat, and a couple of vLLM clusters for in-house inference, mostly for our extraction pipeline.
00:18 Sofia: hi, Sofia, ML lead, focused on prompt engineering and eval suites.
00:24 Tom: Tom infra, I manage the k8s clusters for the vLLM hosts and networking.
00:32 Alex: great, Alex from Redwood, Priya and Marcus with me, we'll walk through how a move could look. Quick ask from our side: what does success look like for you?
00:41 Rajiv: two main things — parity with what we get today from OpenAI/TGI on quality, and predictable cost with lower tail latency than our vLLM p95 now. Also need SSO and audit logs for compliance.
00:54 Priya: totally. When you say parity, do you mean same exact token-level outputs or tolerance for small variation as long as eval metrics hold?
01:04 Sofia: we need eval parity on our rouge/qa metrics and human review for top 200 prompts. Exact token-to-token match isn't required, but behavior needs to be within regression thresholds.
01:16 Marcus: ok, that's doable—we run evaluation harnesses and can reproduce top prompt set on Redwood hosted or dedicated. A few notes on differences: kernel selection and quantization can change low-probability tokens, but we can tune.
01:31 Tom: network question — if we go Dedicated vs Private, what's the difference in egress and VPC setup? we have strict firewall rules.
01:40 Alex: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our infra with private networking options; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed control plane — firewall and peering are yours. We'll send the network runbook.
01:53 Rajiv: security: SOC2?/ISO? KMS? We need encryption at rest + HSM-backed keys for some datasets.
02:02 Alex: We have SOC2 and ISO attestation; support for KMS integrations and HSM for Private deployments. We'll share the security pack after.
02:12 Sofia: about benchmarks — our current setup: OpenAI for chat (few-hundred ms), vLLM on G5s for extraction with avg latency ~220ms p50 and 430ms p95. Cost-savvy wants under $0.01/token equivalent. Can Redwood meet that with quantization + batching?
02:32 Priya: depends on model and sequence lengths; with 8-bit quant (+batching + KV cache) we often reduce per-token cost materially. For strict p95 SLOs you may trade off higher dedicated capacity or smaller batch windows.
02:46 Rajiv: can you run our top-200 prompt set and compare?
02:50 Marcus: yes, we can run exact evals. Two ways: hosted eval run (we provision a sandbox) or Dedicated pilot where you push traffic. Hosted is fastest to start.
03:01 Tom: latency jitter is our biggest worry — vLLM has custom kernels that are tuned for our seq lengths. Will Redwood’s runtime handle that same pattern?
03:12 Priya: we have kernel selection and seq-length aware compiles; we'll need your seq distribution. Also we support model variants and fallback routing to keep latency stable.
03:24 Rajiv: compatibility — we use some TGI-specific tokenizer settings and a few homegrown special tokens in prompts. Will that port cleanly?
03:33 Marcus: tokenizer differences are the usual gotcha. We'll validate on your tokenizer and push a minimal compatibility shim. If there's custom special tokens we can accept them in the prompt header or preprocess.
03:45 Sofia: are there any known regressions when converting from fp16 to quantized int8 on transformer heads? Our QA team saw hallucination increases in a prior migration.
03:57 Priya: hallucination can increase if quantization isn't matched or if calibration corpora miss tail tokens. Our Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles based on representative prompt sets — that's why we ask for your sample prompts.
04:10 Rajiv: talk me through rollout strategy — we can't risk full cutover.
04:15 Alex: typical plan: 1) benchmark parity with eval suite, 2) pilot on non-critical traffic (10%), 3) canary with A/B and automatic fallback to OpenAI if regressions detected, 4) gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring and rollback hooks. We can integrate with your feature flags.
04:33 Tom: what about costs and commitments?
04:36 Alex: Hosted: pay-as-you-go; Dedicated: committed monthly capacity with lower unit costs and SLA; Private: subscription + infra. We'll send a precise pricing comparison.
04:46 Rajiv: any vendor lock-in concerns? We want to avoid tie-in if new models come out.
04:51 Marcus: we support model variants and let you pin versions — switching models is a config change not a rewrite. For on-prem, you control the model artifacts.
04:59 Sofia: I want to run a quick technical deep dive after this discovery — can Priya run the benchmark plan?
05:05 Priya: yes, I'll own the benchmark plan. We'll need token logs, prompt list, and access to the eval labels.
05:13 Rajiv: timeline — if we like the results we want a pilot starting end of November. Is that feasible?
05:20 Alex: yes — schedule depends on your readiness. We'll aim for infra sync next week to lock windows.
05:27 Tom: small nit — the vLLM clusters use a custom batching layer. If we move to Redwood Dedicated, how do you handle steady-state batching vs our burst patterns?
05:38 Priya: Redwood runtime supports dynamic batching with max-latency thresholds and workload-aware autoscaling. For bursty workloads we recommend a small reserved headroom in Dedicated capacity.
05:48 Sofia: documentation question: do you have an eval template / sample JSON for our human reviewers?
05:52 Marcus: yes, we'll share a benchmark template and a sample evaluation spreadsheet.
05:58 Rajiv: any concerns about PII? we process customer PII for some pipelines.
06:03 Alex: for PII we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict VPC and KMS. We'll send data residency and retention options.
06:12 Tom: ok sounds good. One more, SE question — are there any known incompatibilities with our internal streaming RPCs?
06:20 Priya: we support streaming and function calling; we may need a small adapt layer for custom RPC. Should be straightforward.
06:31 Alex: great. Let's recap next steps.
06:34 Rajiv: yeah please recap.
06:36 Alex: Action items — Redwood: share Dedicated pricing and security pack, SE to draft benchmark plan, Redwood to provision hosted sandbox if desired; IronPeak: share prompts and token logs, Tom to coordinate infra windows.
06:50 Rajiv: perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll review and aim to get that export by Friday.
06:57 Alex: thanks folks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra sync and benchmark run.
07:03 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings around acronym TGI -> 'tea gee eye' in transcript and vLLM sometimes appears as 'vee LLM' or 'v-llm', some names may be slightly off in the auto-transcript.
